Verdict:


Arms: No need for a real rig. Just the ability to go from straight to bent. Everything can be parented at the shoulder to an empty so it can be rotated and lengthened or shortened. This should be totally fine for all shots besides the cockpit shot. For that one-off we should parent the hands to the steering yoke rather than counteranimate.


Legs: Similar to arms. For swinging and running they can be like the arms. Swap asset when he hits the ground so they are anchored at the feet.


Face: Most shots are so fast we shouldn't need real facial animation. When he spits out the seed (and puts it back in) it will take a lot of work, but it can be done with shape keys. I would recommend that we separate the head from the body so we don't have to paint weights or anything that would make things more complicated.


Body/Jacket: If we separate the head and body we can parent the jacket/bandoleer to the body. The jacket needs the ability to flap around. I think shape keys will probably work ok. This will probably just require a different treatment for each shot.


Bottom line: We should set up a master version of Black Hamster with the body and head separated and parented to their own empties. Simple arm and leg "rigs" using simple parenting and shape keys. Face can be animated with shape keys.


Still Unknown:


The shading and UVs need to be worked on. I don't want to get too far along with each shot being set up differently for animation and then figure out the shading.
